core_themes.name: High buy-out use in Target Period 1
core_themes.claim: In TP1 just under half of target units (49%) used buy-out and 14% of those missing targets left the scheme, which suggests the £12/tCO2e price gave a weak incentive to meet targets.

core_themes.name: Original buy-out price rationale
core_themes.claim: The £12/tCO2e price set in 2012 was meant to balance a strong incentive to abate against financial and competitiveness impacts on participants, with targets challenging but achievable and buy-out as an alternative route to compliance.

core_themes.name: Limits of the TP1 evidence
core_themes.claim: TP1 data cover only the first of four target periods and buy-out use is expected to be higher in TP1 because of time-lags in abatement measures, so later periods may differ.

diagnosis.note: The overall diagnosis of a weak incentive is largely inferred from TP1 buy-out use rather than stated outright.

core_themes.name: Raise buy-out price in line with RPI to £14
core_themes.claim: The preferred option is to raise the buy-out price to £14/tCO2e for TP3 and TP4, which keeps it constant in real terms, matches the CRC allowance price approach, and reflects the higher CCL discount and high TP1 buy-out use.

core_themes.name: Rejection of alternative price options
core_themes.claim: A rise to £17 was rejected over competitiveness impacts and a CRC link that ends in 2019, while keeping £12 was rejected because the CCL discount has grown and TP1 buy-out use was high.

core_themes.name: Balance of incentive and competitiveness
core_themes.claim: A higher price gives a sharper incentive to meet targets but must be weighed against competitiveness impacts, and respondents' views (16 of 20 opposed a change, citing certainty and investment) are acknowledged while evidence is still sought.

proposal.note: The proposal is a consultation on three price options with a stated preference; no cost-benefit estimates are given.

core_themes.name: Decision process and timing
core_themes.claim: The Government will consider consultation responses and announce in the autumn whether the buy-out price will be revised for TP3 and TP4.

implementation.note: Implementation is only a brief next-steps statement about how the decision will be made, with no delivery method, evidence or costs.
